description: I am a solo participant passionate about AI, scientific research, and space exploration. Through Flame in Freefall, I aim to build an AI-powered platform that analyzes NASA’s microgravity combustion data, identifies patterns, and makes scientific insights more accessible.
summary:
Flame in Freefall 🔥 is an AI-assisted scientific research platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its primary goal is to understand how fire behaves in microgravity environments, where combustion differs significantly from Earth due to reduced buoyancy and convection.

The platform uses NASA's real microgravity combustion experiment data to analyse flame behaviour, compare experimental conditions, identify patterns, and visualise scientific findings. It also includes an AI research assistant that explains complex combustion concepts and helps users explore experiments.

An additional researcher contribution module allows researchers to submit new experimental records, findings, and references, with verification and source tracking to maintain scientific credibility.

Ultimately, Flame in Freefall aims to make microgravity combustion research more accessible and contribute to safer future space missions to the Moon and Mars.
details: Project Name: Flame in Freefall 🔥 Project Overview: An AI-assisted scientific research platform designed to study and understand combustion behaviour in microgravity environments. Challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Objective: To analyse how flames behave in space and understand the differences between combustion on Earth and in microgravity. Key Features: * Experiment Explorer – Explore NASA's microgravity combustion experiment data. * AI Research Assistant – Understand scientific findings through AI-powered explanations. * Combustion Visualisation – Display flame behaviour through interactive graphs and visualisations. * Experiment Comparison – Compare experiments based on fuel, temperature, pressure and oxygen concentration where data is available. * Researcher Contribution Module – Allow researchers to submit experiment records, findings, documents and references. * Fire Safety Insights – Support research into fire behaviour and spacecraft safety. Technology Stack: React.js, Vite, Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Pandas, NumPy and AI/ML technologies. Target Users: Researchers, scientists, students, educators and space enthusiasts. Expected Impact: Make NASA combustion research more accessible, help researchers identify patterns in experimental data, and support future spacecraft fire-safety research for missions to the Moon and Mars. Core Vision: Transform complex microgravity combustion data into accessible, interactive and evidence-based scientific insights.
